chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The one in Ihram should not apply kohl except for pain. And he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with applying kohl while you are in Ihram, provided it does not contain perfume whose scent is found. But as for adornment, then no.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يَكْتَحِلْ: To apply kohl (ithmid) to the eyes

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram apply kohl to their eyes?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between therapeutic and cosmetic use of kohl during Ihram, emphasizing that the prohibition applies specifically to substances with detectable fragrance used for adornment. It reflects the Shia scholarly principle that minor adornments are permissible if they lack the scent that signifies luxury or beauty, thereby preserving the state of spiritual simplicity required for pilgrimage.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

The one in Ihraam cannot apply Kohl except for pain’. And heasws said: ‘There is no problem with if you apply Kohl and you are in Ihraam, with what does not happen to have perfume in it or its aroma is not found. But, as for adornment, so no’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

One in the state of Ihram must not use kohl unless it is to cure pain.’ He (the Imam) has said, ‘Using kohl which does not have any perfume while one is in the state of Ihram is not harmful, however, for beautification it is not permissible.’”
